notes.supply_chain_2026_08_29: PR #166: gitleaks flagged the I-01 demonstration's restated 64-hex probe as generic-api-key (correct -- a synthetic value and a real one are the same bytes to a scanner); fixed by using the probe already declared in CREDENTIAL_PROBES, with no allowlist entry and no scanner config change. cargo-audit failed on chacha20 0.10.1 being yanked upstream, which is not this branch's doing; bumped to 0.10.2 in Cargo.lock rather than added to the RUSTSEC ignore list.
notes.contracts_boxes_2026_08_29: Phase 10's two contracts/ boxes are annotated and deliberately LEFT UNCHECKED. I-13's substance is delivered (contracts/ is the source, versioned in contracts/index.json, drift-gated by check_contracts_single_source.py), but the boxes say 'duplicates deleted' and two copies of five files still exist: drift is impossible, deletion has not happened. The remaining move is an audited engine change, not the production gate. The second box also names an 'approval' schema that exists nowhere in the tree (T-021).
notes.route_budgets_2026_08_29: T-041: the bundle gate budgeted one entry and left 23 lazily-loaded route chunks (256.7 KB gzip) with no ceiling, while Phase 10 asked for a performance gate over all 22 pages. perf-budget.json now has a routes section and check_bundle_budget.py enforces it bidirectionally; a route's cost is its closure minus the entry's. The two roadmap rows stay UNTICKED for one word -- 'production' -- because axe runs in jsdom, not against the built app; the computed-style (real Chromium) workflow already has the browser.
notes.axe_real_browser_2026_08_29: T-042: axe now runs in real Chromium with CSS and color-contrast enabled over 23 pages x 2 states x 2 themes plus the shell and the command palette (98 checks), which answers the word 'production' in Phase 10's a11y row. It found 11 defects, 10 of them light-theme. Three preconditions had to be fixed first: axe-core 3.5.6 was hoisted by @types/jest-axe and graded the app by ARIA 1.1 (pinned to 4.10.2); the light-theme axis was vacuous because AppProvider overwrites data-theme from an effect (green twice before a guard caught it); and entrance animations had to settle. contrast-pairs.json is now asserted to mirror tokens.ts -- it never was. Static checks 56 -> 64. Both Phase 10 a11y/perf rows are ticked.
notes.aios_palette_contract_2026_08_29: T-043: contrast-pairs.json now carries BOTH palettes (14 new pairs, 92 checks, was 64) and the mirror assertion routes by family -- aios-* against aios.css, everything else against tokens.ts. --hi is declared in both :root blocks and painted nowhere, so no pair names it; the first draft did and produced a real 4.32:1 about a background no page has. The -tint exemption is narrowed to the aios family, because --menq-color-<name>-tint are real tokens and a blanket rule would undo T-042.
notes.t040_timeout_2026_08_29: T-040 closed by measurement: GroupChat.readout's value arrives 200 ms after mount in isolation against Testing Library's 1000 ms asyncUtilTimeout, while vitest.config.ts had already raised testTimeout to 30 s for the same reason -- the suite raised the timeout it knew about and left the one that fires. asyncUtilTimeout is 5000 ms now; neither --retry nor singleFork was used. The isolated latency is pinned at 1000 ms separately so a real slowdown still fails, and a second test proves the ceiling is in force. 3 consecutive full runs 757/757.
notes.dead_tokens_2026_08_29: T-044: check_c1_tokens asserts every var(--x) resolves; nothing asserted the reverse. 20 of 149 custom properties were declared and read by nothing (the naive scan said 24 -- four were BEM modifiers). Six deleted as T-033 residue, nine pinned by §C.1 (including --hi, which answers T-042's open note), five allowed by name with reasons. tools/check_dead_tokens.py is wired into CI; the by-name-not-by-prefix property had no test until a mutant proved it.
